question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the exact solutions in radians to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ for $-\pi \le x<\pi ,$ are

${x}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We divide both sides of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{\pi }{3}$ is inside the given domain, one solution is ${x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

To find another solution in the domain, we subtract $\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\pi =-\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{2\pi }{3},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$
